# Normal Approximation for Poisson Probability

## Setting Up the Problem

Given $Y \sim \text{Pois}(n)$, we know:
- $E[Y] = n$
- $\operatorname{Var}(Y) = n$

We need to estimate $P\big[|Y - n| \geq 2\sqrt{n}\big]$.

## Applying the CLT (Normal Approximation)

For large $n$, the Poisson distribution is well-approximated by a Normal distribution:

$$Y \approx \mathcal{N}(n,\; n)$$

**Standardizing.** Define the standardized variable:

$$Z = \frac{Y - n}{\sqrt{n}} \;\;\dot\sim\;\; \mathcal{N}(0,1)$$

The event $|Y - n| \geq 2\sqrt{n}$ is equivalent to:

$$\frac{|Y - n|}{\sqrt{n}} \geq 2 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad |Z| \geq 2$$

## Computing the Probability

$$P\big[|Y - n| \geq 2\sqrt{n}\big] \;\approx\; P(|Z| \geq 2) = P(Z \geq 2) + P(Z \leq -2)$$

By symmetry of the standard normal:

$$P(|Z| \geq 2) = 2\,P(Z \geq 2) = 2\big(1 - \Phi(2)\big)$$

Using the standard normal table:

$$\Phi(2) \approx 0.9772 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 1 - \Phi(2) \approx 0.0228$$

$$P(|Z| \geq 2) \approx 2 \times 0.0228 = 0.0456$$

## Result

$$\boxed{0.0456}$$
